thread:
incident-bot Service alert: p99 latency spike on /v1/generate across eu-west-1. Details: KV cache eviction rate up 18x, batching queues backing up, paging increasing.

alice.chen Yeah seeing the spike on the dashboard. p95 jumped to 2.4s, p99 ~6s. Errors are 502s from frontend gateway.

miguel.torres I think this is the continuous-batching regression we rolled last night — batch_sizing_policy default changed to 'aggressive' for seqs>256.

priya.kapoor @miguel.torres can you confirm which canary rolled?

miguel.torres Canary tag: release/2026-03-12-batch-opt. I reverted on the node we control and the queue cleared a bit but cache eviction still high.

ben.oneill Any signs of large KV cache blowups? I see mem pressure and frequent page faults on the host.

kate.green Paging counts: host-3 had a 3x increase in page-in rates starting at 05:12 UTC. KV cache size doubled due to a leaked prefix retention in the new batching code.

alice.chen Customer impact: several enterprise tenants reported degraded latency and a handful saw 429s during bursts. No data loss.

priya.kapoor On-call handoff: I'm the primary oncall until 06:00 UTC, can take lead. @kate.green do you have a mitigation plan?

kate.green Short term: 1) revert batch_sizing_policy to previous 'conservative' for the canary and roll to edge nodes. 2) force-kill stale KV prefixes older than 12h (careful). 3) throttle long-running requests (seq>1024) to the lower-priority pool to avoid starving short requests.

miguel.torres I'm pushing a hotfix to rollback the change and will run it on a small slice first. Command: 
```
kubectl -n inference set image deployment/batcher batcher=redwood/batcher:2026-03-11-rc
```

ben.oneill I prepared a script to delete overly-retained prefixes: 
```
python tools/kv_prune.py --older-than 12h --namespace eu-west-1 --dry-run
```
Run with --force after we validate.

alice.chen Kate, can we quickly change the scheduler fairness weights to prioritize small requests? That might cut p99 for typical interactive calls.

kate.green Yes. Adjusting scheduler policy now: 
```
POST /admin/scheduler/config HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:9000
Content-Type: application/json

{"fairness_policy":"size_weighted","short_weight":1.7,"long_weight":0.5}
```
Applying... done. Monitoring.

incident-bot Acknowledged by priya.kapoor, severity set to P1. Notifying infra and SRE.

(2m pause)

miguel.torres Hotfix rollout started to 5% traffic. I'll watch KV eviction metrics and batching latencies.

ben.oneill After the scheduler tweak p95 dropped to 1.1s on the canary hosts. p99 improved slightly.

kate.green KV eviction rate decreased ~45% on canary hosts after rollback began. Paging still elevated on one host.

alice.chen Customer update draft: "We experienced a transient increase in latency affecting some requests in eu-west-1 due to a regression in a batching optimization. We have rolled back the change, adjusted scheduler weights to protect interactive traffic, and are pruning stale KV prefixes. We're monitoring and will follow up with root cause." Approve to send? :thumbsup: :thumbsdown:

priya.kapoor Approve. Send to affected tenant contacts and post a note in #customer-impact.

miguel.torres Rollout to 30% now. I see the remaining paging host is saturated with long sequences. I'm going to drain long-request pool and shift to dedicated nodes.

kate.green Draining long pool: `curl -XPOST http://router/admin/drain?pool=long-seq&timeout=30s`

(confirmation)

ben.oneill Done. Long sequences are now routed to dedicated long-pool nodes which have larger cache limits.

alice.chen Monitoring the global p99: trending down. Gateway 502s cleared up.

incident-bot Pager cleared for priya.kapoor at 05:48 UTC — incident still active with mitigations in progress.

priya.kapoor Oncall note: assigned runbook "batching-regression" and added checklist steps taken: rollback, scheduler tweak, KV prune, long-pool drain.

miguel.torres Rollout to 100% complete at 05:55 UTC. All batcher instances on release/2026-03-11-rc.

kate.green Executed prefix prune with --force on the remaining hosts. Freed ~22GB across cluster. Paging rates returned to baseline.

alice.chen Customer impact summary for postmortem: "Latency increases (p95/p99) and transient 429/502 errors for some tenants in eu-west-1 from 05:12–05:55 UTC; primary cause: a batching config regression that increased prefix retention and allowed long requests to monopolize batch scheduler, causing KV cache pressure and host paging. Mitigations — immediate rollback, scheduler fairness tuning, routing long sequences to dedicated pool, pruning stale prefixes."

priya.kapoor I'll start the incident report and share an initial timeline. Assigning owners: root cause analysis — @miguel.torres; long-request routing improvements — @ben.oneill; KV cache guardrails (auto-prune/limits) — @kate.green; monitoring alerts refinement — @alice.chen.

alice.chen Can we add an automated check in CI that prevents batch_sizing_policy changes without a perf eval?

miguel.torres Yep adding a gate. Will open a PR with test harness results and link in the postmortem.

deploy-bot Deployment: release/2026-03-11-rc fully rolled at 05:55 UTC to cluster eu-west-1.

priya.kapoor Closing notes: keep monitoring for 2 hours and then transition to follow-up task force in #eng-runtime for RCA. Thanks all for quick turnaround. :heart:

alice.chen +1 thanks team.

(End of thread)
